title: Prioritized locality stickiness with capacity feedback loop
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a routing policy that prefers local region endpoints (stickiness) for low-latency traffic but adapts dynamically when local capacity is constrained. The policy should: 1) maintain session or token affinity when possible to maximize cache/KV reuse and low p99 latency, 2) detect capacity pressure and gracefully shed or re-route traffic to secondary regions according to SLO tiers, and 3) surface clear signals for circuit breakers and orchestrated evacuations without cascading failures.
strategy_summary: Introduce a capacity-feedback loop that augments locality affinity with a soft-decay mechanism. Affinity weights are computed per token/customer bucket and decay when local availability or queueing latency exceeds threshold. When decay triggers, requests are probabilistically steered to a precomputed failover set prioritized by SLO compatibility and cost. Circuit-breaker thresholds and token-bucket ejection work together to avoid thundering herd when downstream capacity fluctuates.
acceptance_criteria: Latency: 95th percentile tail for regional-affinitized traffic remains within 10% of baseline when local capacity > 60%
Failover: Under simulated local saturation, 90% of overflowed traffic is routed to secondary regions within 250ms decision window
Shed behavior: When global capacity low, token-bucket shedding reduces accepted QPS smoothly with <5% variance in aggregate throughput per minute
Observability: Console dashboard shows affinity weight trend, local capacity signal, and circuit-breaker state in real time
Rollout: Feature flag gating and canary to 10% of customers with automatic rollback on increased p99 by >20%
plan: Prototype affinity weight calculator (in-serving) that consumes queue length, GPU util, and KV cache hit rate
Add a capacity signal exporter and a standardized local_capacity metric to the control plane
Implement soft-decay and probabilistic failover in request director with feature flag
Build token-bucket ejection layer and tie to circuit-breaker state machine
Create dashboards and alerts, run staged chaos tests (network partitions, cold-cache, rapid load spike), iterate
Canary rollout to 10% and full rollout after two weeks of stability metrics
notes: Tradeoffs: Strong stickiness preserves latency but concentrates load; soft-decay balances cache reuse vs local overload risk
Design decision: Use probabilistic re-routing rather than hard pinning to avoid synchronized migrations and reduce cache stampede risk
Circuit breakers: Two-tier breakers planned: 1) local short-window breaker to protect local queueing, 2) region-level breaker to prevent cross-region saturation
Ejection strategy: Token-bucket per-customer with burst allowance; when bucket emptied requests are demoted to lower SLO routes or shed according to policy
Compatibility: Must interoperate with existing autoscaler signals and multi-region cost-aware routing matrix
Performance: Affinity calculation kept O(1) per request; changes limited to director module to minimize runtime boundary changes
